groupAudit.note: Group re-audit of adversarial-environments after repair cycle 2 of run foundations-2-repair-1 (owned: adversaries, threat-models, byzantine-behavior, censorship, collusion; strategic-behavior dual-role and fixed, read only for boundaries). Scoped to the two repaired sentences and what depends on them; adversaries, threat-models and censorship are unchanged since their accepted group audit and were re-read only against the repairs, with no material defect found. group-signals printed 0 signals, so there are no resolutions. No blocking finding: no contradiction between members, no split or reservation crossed, no member explaining what another claims. (1) Byzantine Behavior, paragraph 9 ('Rotation on a schedule limits how long one holder's choices or silence can last; replacement on a timeout limits how long it can stay silent, and replacement on evidence of misbehavior removes it only for what can be proven, so a holder that stays responsive and makes only valid choices may keep its role under either'). Against Censorship: Censorship's 'an includer whose turn ends can only delay an action unless those after it also leave it out' and 'an action left out by one proposer can be picked up by a later one' agree with rotation bounding one holder's choices; the repaired sentence says nothing about inclusion paths, exclusion means, deadlines or motives, and Censorship stays named only for the choice of what to include. Censorship's time-bound point (a delay within the remaining window can cause a loss later inclusion does not undo) is consistent, since the record says rotation limits how long the holder chooses, not that it prevents harm. The angles differ (replacing role holders in general vs alternative paths around a step), so the shared idea follows the claims. Against Adversaries: replacement on a timeout and the final sentence on partial synchrony agree with Adversaries' formulation (unbounded delay until an unknown stabilization time, bounded after), which is why a slow correct holder can be removed and a Byzantine one acting within the timeouts is not; no adversary power or scheduling is explained. 'Evidence' and 'can be proven' keep Byzantine Behavior's own sense (statements a third party can verify), and attribution remains its territory alone. (2) Collusion, paragraph 3 ('no participants acting together controlling more than a bounded share'). It now agrees with the Adversarial Environments parent ('Participants who are each within bounds can act as one: pooling resources past a threshold') instead of contradicting it, and names the bound without restating the pooling arithmetic. It agrees with Adversaries' single-coordinating-adversary convention and its condition 'that no more participants are corrupted than the model allows', a bound on what the coordinating set controls, and with Adversaries' handoff of real agreements to Collusion. It agrees with Threat Models, which lists agreements made outside the protocol as a recurring exclusion concerning Collusion: a model can either exclude such agreements or rest on a joint bound they can defeat, and the record's 'A protocol often has no rule against an agreement made outside it' is consistent with both. No colluders are counted against a threshold, so the Trust Distribution reservation is not crossed; the Sybil split is untouched. Convergence: the repairs changed no structure, opening or paragraph count; the prior group audit's convergence judgment stands (shared openings only in Adversaries and Threat Models, below the signal threshold; all prose, fitting conditions-and-distinctions concepts; arcs differ). Advisory: (a) Collusion's repaired phrase stacks two participles; the model's wording ('a bound on the share that participants acting together control') would read more smoothly, and the sentence could say the bound is defeated when the colluders' combined share exceeds it, which the paragraph's 'Collusion undermines something when...' already conditions; (b) Byzantine Behavior's 'how long one holder's choices or silence can last' could be read as the persistence of a choice's effects, which Censorship shows can outlast the holder's turn; 'how long one holder keeps choosing or stays silent' would be clearer; (c) Byzantine Behavior's rotation clause and Censorship's 'an includer whose turn ends can only delay' touch the same idea from different claims, acceptable; (d) the prior group audit's advisories (Adversaries/Threat Models bound clause, common-rule sanctions example in Censorship and Collusion, omission cover in Censorship and Byzantine Behavior, Collusion's trustless contracts vs Strategic Behavior's bribe contract, shared openings of Adversaries and Threat Models) still apply unchanged.
